messages.subject: xlsx version 0.4.0 to be released soon
messages.subject_clean: xlsx version 0.4.0 to be released soon
messages.body_plain:
I'm currently testing and putting the latest touches on version 0.4.0
of package xlsx.

There will be BACKWARDS INCOMPATIBLE CHANGES related to cell styles!

A complete rewrite of functionality to deal with cell styles has been
added.  Although I want to minimize API breaking changes, I belive
that these changes are for the better as the old function
createCellStyle had a whopping 11 arguments and was still incomplete.
The new functionality defines an S3 object CellStyle on which you can
"add" DataFormat, Font, Fill, Border, Alignment, Protection.

Other small changes are in the works too.  Please check out the
development version of the package from
http://code.google.com/p/rexcel/

On the note of backward compatibility, I don't want to promise
anything as the package is still young.  But as more people start
using the package, the API will freeze and if breaking changes are
contemplated, a clear deprecation path will be provided.

Adrian

messages.subject_clean: xlsx version 0.4.0 to be released soon
messages.body_plain:
I completely understand the issue with backwards compatibility, though
if there's any way to keep existing methods as-is, then create new
methods for the new fancy stuff, that could help the transition.

My biggest obstacle to using this package for everything I do in Excel
is data volume.  Exporting a table with 30,000 rows takes 10-15' easy,
and on a machine with reasonably high specs (12 cores, 32 GB memory.)
Obviously it isn't using all that during export, but I do have some
Java options set to increase above the defaults.  Optimizing the code
is likely tricky because it would need to become vectorized code, but
I thought I'd just say that while I love this package, and have
written my own wrapper to help automate exporting fancy Excel tables,
I can't use the package because any moderately-sized files just take
too long.

A side-note, the code I wrote to automate export of fancy tables is
pretty helpful for me: I can specify highlight column, number/integer/
wordWrap/pvalue columns, and it has preset formats which will
alternate lighter-darker columns, color-code values above thresholds
(like significant P-values), word-wrap certain columns, auto-size
certain columns, and fix the width of the word-wrapped and any other
user-specified columns.  However without any user-defined options it
has pretty sensible defaults.  The only thing I've yet to add is
autodetection of column types for any columns not defined by the
user.  The method is called writeXlsx().

messages.subject: Re: Package "xlsx"
messages.body_plain:
Hercules,

I'm CC'in the list "R-package-xlsx" where I would like to track these conversations.

To reply to your questions.

1)  You're doing everything right, but setRowBreak has a bug on the java POI library.  It seems to be fixed in the current beta version 3.8 beta 5.  I don't want to add a beta version to CRAN, but you can easily download it and drop it in the xlsxjars package.  It should work.

2)  I cannot reproduce it.  I'm using both styles, in fact I favor / because it's the same on Linux.

3)  You need to use .jshort(1) to convert to a short.  Look at the sources for PrintSetup for example.

Best,
Adrian

Also, the package will get a significant face lift this weekend (I'm releasing version 0.4.0).  You can get the development version at http://code.google.com/p/rexcel/

>
>
> Question 1 (see attachment, Pagebreaks.R)
>
> I cannot seem to get the setRowBreak function to insert an actual row break. The attached code is supposed to create a sheet of 100 rows, and insert page breaks at 20,40,60,80. getRowBreaks shows that the row breaks have been correctly inserted, however when the file is opened, only one page break after row 50 is present (and this is the automatic Excel version). Am I doing something wrong, or is there some limitation that I should be aware of.
>
> This is quite a critical feature for me, since my reports are a bunch of tables, and it looks silly if the page break is in the middle of a table.
>
>
> Question 2 (again see attachment, Pagebreaks.R)
> Consider the lines
>
> saveWorkbook(wb, "c:\\test.xlsx")
> saveWorkbook(wb, "c:/test.xlsx")

> The first line works - and the second line does not. I am assuming that this is because of the underlying Java? I am not too worried about this as there is a workaround - though it took me some time to figure this out.
>
> Question 3
>
>
> I am trying to call sheet$getPrintSetup()$setFitWidth(1) (where sheet is the object as in Pagebreaks.R) - however the requirement is that the 1 must be a short.
>
> I tried
>
> library(R.utils)
> sheet$getPrintSetup()$setFitWidth(Java$asShort(1))
>
>
> but then I get
> "Error in ls(envir = envir, all.names = private)
>  invalid 'envir' argument"
>
> Again calling upon your greater experience - is there anything else that I can try?
>
>
> Thank you very much for your time, and I apologise for the any inconvenience that I may have caused.
>
> Regards
> Hercules

messages.subject: Re: xlsx version 0.4.0 to be released soon
messages.subject_clean: xlsx version 0.4.0 to be released soon
messages.body_plain:
James,

I believe that the speed issues have improved considerably in version 0.4.0.   I've added two new functions addDataFrame to write a data.frame to a sheet, and a readColumns to read a data.frame from a sheet.  Function addDataFrame allows you to style each column of your data.frame as you write it.

If you have to do cell by cell style customization, then these functions won't help you as they work by column.  Maybe the way to go in your case is by conditional formatting
http://poi.apache.org/spreadsheet/quick-guide.html#ConditionalFormatting
but I haven't tried it as I didn't need it, and I was very busy upgrading the package.

If you want to check the new version, it's at http://code.google.com/p/rexcel/

If everything goes as planned, I intend to upload to CRAN this weekend.

Adrian

messages.subject: version 0.4.1 released
messages.body_plain:
Hello,

Minor changes from 0.4.0.  I fixed a corner case for addDataFrame so that it works on existing sheets not only on new sheets.

Should be up on CRAN in the next few days.  For the impatient, I've uploaded the new version on http://code.google.com/p/rexcel/

Best,
Adrian
